title: Limit presentation of a tower of local rings essentially of finite presentation with a finitely presented module
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$, $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$, $(S',\mathfrak m_{S'})$ be local rings and $R\xrightarrow{\alpha}S\xrightarrow{\beta}S'$ local homomorphisms ($\alpha(\mathfrak m)\subseteq\mathfrak m_S$, $\beta(\mathfrak m_S)\subseteq\mathfrak m_{S'}$). Assume that $S$ and $S'$ are essentially of finite presentation over $R$ (via $\alpha$, resp. $\beta\circ\alpha$): each is isomorphic, as an $R$-algebra, to a localization $W^{-1}B$ of a finitely presented $R$-algebra $B$ [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra] at a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq B$. Let $M$ be a finitely presented $S'$-module ($M\cong\operatorname{coker}(S'^{\oplus s}\to S'^{\oplus t})$ for some $s,t\ge0$ and some $S'$-linear map). Then there exist a nonempty directed set $(\Lambda,\le)$ and the following data: for every $\lambda\in\Lambda$, local rings $(R_\lambda,\mathfrak p_\lambda)$, $S_\lambda$, $S'_\lambda$, local homomorphisms $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$ and an $S'_\lambda$-module $M_\lambda$; for $\lambda\le\mu$, local homomorphisms $R_\lambda\to R_\mu$, $S_\lambda\to S_\mu$, $S'_\lambda\to S'_\mu$ commuting with the maps $R_\lambda\to S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$ and $R_\mu\to S_\mu\to S'_\mu$, and an additive map $M_\lambda\to M_\mu$ with $(sx)\mapsto\bar s\,\bar x$ for $s\in S'_\lambda$ (bars denoting images), all equal to the identity for $\lambda=\mu$ and compatible with composition; and for every $\lambda$ local homomorphisms $R_\lambda\to R$, $S_\lambda\to S$, $S'_\lambda\to S'$ commuting with $\alpha$, $\beta$ and the transition maps, and additive maps $M_\lambda\to M$, semilinear over $S'_\lambda\to S'$ and compatible with the transition maps; such that: (1) $R$, $S$, $S'$ with these maps are colimits [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the rings $R_\lambda$, $S_\lambda$, $S'_\lambda$ in the category of commutative rings, and $M$ is the colimit of the abelian groups $M_\lambda$; (2) $R_\lambda$ is essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, $S_\lambda$ is essentially of finite type over $R_\lambda$ and $S'_\lambda$ is essentially of finite type over $S_\lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]; (3) $M_\lambda$ is a finitely generated $S'_\lambda$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] (indeed the cokernel of a matrix $S'^{\oplus s}_\lambda\to S'^{\oplus t}_\lambda$); (4) for all $\lambda\le\mu$ the ring maps $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S_\mu$ and $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to S'_\mu$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\bar x\,y$, are localizations at some multiplicative subsets (a ring map $C\to D$ is a *localization of $C$ at* a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq C$ if every element of $W$ maps to a unit of $D$, every element of $D$ is the image of $c$ times the inverse of the image of $w$ for some $c\in C$, $w\in W$, and $c\mapsto0$ implies $wc=0$ for some $w\in W$), and the map $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'_\mu\to M_\mu$, $x\otimes y\mapsto y\,\bar x$, is an isomorphism of $S'_\mu$-modules; (5) for every $\lambda$ the ring maps $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to S$ and $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to S'$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\bar x\,y$, are localizations at some multiplicative subsets, and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'\to M$, $x\otimes y\mapsto y\,\bar x$, is an isomorphism of $S'$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), first paragraph and the first sentences of the second ('With these choices, we have for each $\lambda_3\le\lambda\le\mu$ that $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S_\mu$ is a localization, $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to S'_\mu$ is a localization, and the map $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'_\mu\to M_\mu$ is an isomorphism'), a construction made 'as in the proof of' Lemma Tag 00QV (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-presentation, line 32346) and Lemma Tag 00QX (lemma-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation, line 32427), whose proofs end 'We leave it to the reader to see that this works'; R is written as a colimit of local rings essentially of finite type over Z as in the proof of Lemma Tag 00QU (lemma-limit-essentially-finite-type, line 32273). Clause (5) is the form of the last sentence of the proof of 00R7 that is true ('S = S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R' there; only a localization in general). The construction uses that S' is essentially of finite presentation over S, which Stacks does not state as a lemma.

proof.text: (The base system.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-colimit-essentially-finite-type-over-z] to the local ring $(R,\mathfrak m)$: we get a nonempty directed set $(\Lambda,\le)$, local rings $(R_\lambda,\mathfrak p_\lambda)$, essentially of finite type over $\mathbf Z$, local transition homomorphisms $r_{\mu\lambda}:R_\lambda\to R_\mu$ (identities for $\lambda=\mu$, compatible with composition) and local homomorphisms $\pi_\lambda:R_\lambda\to R$ compatible with them, such that $(R,(\pi_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda})$ is a colimit of $(R_\lambda)$ in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit].

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), first paragraph: 'As in the proof of Lemma 00QV we may first write $R=\colim R_\lambda$ as a directed colimit of local $\mathbf Z$-algebras which are essentially of finite type'

proof.text: (The middle ring.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation-over-system] to the system of step 1 ($A_\lambda=R_\lambda$, $a_{\mu\lambda}=r_{\mu\lambda}$, $A=R$, $\pi_\lambda$), to $T=S$ with the local homomorphism $\tau=\alpha$ (by hypothesis $S$ is essentially of finite presentation over $R$ via $\alpha$, in the sense of that node), and to the module $N=0$ (the cokernel of $S^{\oplus0}\to S^{\oplus0}$, so finitely presented). We get $\lambda_1\in\Lambda$ and, on $\Lambda_1=\{\lambda\ge\lambda_1\}$, local rings $S_\lambda$, local homomorphisms $\rho_\lambda:R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$, local transition homomorphisms $s_{\mu\lambda}:S_\lambda\to S_\mu$ with $s_{\mu\lambda}\rho_\lambda=\rho_\mu r_{\mu\lambda}$, and local homomorphisms $\kappa_\lambda:S_\lambda\to S$ with $\kappa_\lambda\rho_\lambda=\alpha\pi_\lambda$ and $\kappa_\mu s_{\mu\lambda}=\kappa_\lambda$, such that $(S,(\kappa_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_1})$ is a colimit of $(S_\lambda)_{\Lambda_1}$ in commutative rings, $S_\lambda$ is essentially of finite type over $R_\lambda$ via $\rho_\lambda$, and for $\lambda_1\le\lambda\le\mu$ the maps $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S_\mu$, $x\otimes y\mapsto s_{\mu\lambda}(x)\rho_\mu(y)$, and $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to S$, $x\otimes y\mapsto\kappa_\lambda(x)\alpha(y)$, are localizations at some multiplicative subsets (clauses (1), (2), (4), (5) of that node; the module data, all zero, are discarded).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), first paragraph: 'Next, we may assume that for some $\lambda_1\in\Lambda$ there exist $f_{j,\lambda_1}\in R_{\lambda_1}[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ such that $S=\colim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_1}S_\lambda$, with $S_\lambda=(R_\lambda[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_{1,\lambda},\dots,f_{u,\lambda}))_{\mathfrak q_\lambda}$' (the construction of the proof of Lemma Tag 00QV, line 32346)

proof.text: ($S'$ is essentially of finite presentation over $S$.) By hypothesis $S\cong W^{-1}B$ as $R$-algebras with $B$ a finitely presented $R$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]; a presentation $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_u)\cong B$ is in particular a surjection of $R$-algebras $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]\to B$, so $B$ is of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and $S$ is essentially of finite type over $R$ via $\alpha$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. By hypothesis $S'$ is essentially of finite presentation over $R$ via $\beta\circ\alpha$. Hence, by [lem-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-presentation-over-intermediate] (with $\varphi=\alpha$, $\psi=\beta$), $S'$ is isomorphic as an $S$-algebra (via $\beta$) to a localization $V^{-1}P'$ of a finitely presented $S$-algebra $P'$ at a multiplicative subset $V\subseteq P'$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), first paragraph, where $S'$ is written as $(S_\lambda[y_1,\dots,y_m]/(\bar g_{1,\lambda},\dots,\bar g_{v,\lambda}))_{\bar{\mathfrak q}'_\lambda}$ in the colimit, i.e. as a localization of a finitely presented $S$-algebra (used there without statement)

proof.text: (The top ring and the module.) The set $\Lambda_1$ of step 2 is a nonempty directed set ($\lambda_1\in\Lambda_1$, and an upper bound in $\Lambda$ of two elements of $\Lambda_1$ lies in $\Lambda_1$). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation-over-system] to the system $A_\lambda=S_\lambda$ ($\lambda\in\Lambda_1$) with transition maps $s_{\mu\lambda}$, $A=S$ with the maps $\kappa_\lambda$ (local rings, local maps, colimit: step 2), to $T=S'$ with the local homomorphism $\tau=\beta$ ($S'$ is essentially of finite presentation over $S$ by step 3), and to the $S'$-module $N=M$, finitely presented by hypothesis. We get $\lambda_2\in\Lambda_1$ and, on $\Lambda_2=\{\lambda\in\Lambda_1:\lambda\ge\lambda_2\}=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:\lambda\ge\lambda_2\}$, local rings $S'_\lambda$, local homomorphisms $\sigma_\lambda:S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$, local transition homomorphisms $s'_{\mu\lambda}:S'_\lambda\to S'_\mu$ with $s'_{\mu\lambda}\sigma_\lambda=\sigma_\mu s_{\mu\lambda}$, local homomorphisms $\kappa'_\lambda:S'_\lambda\to S'$ with $\kappa'_\lambda\sigma_\lambda=\beta\kappa_\lambda$ and $\kappa'_\mu s'_{\mu\lambda}=\kappa'_\lambda$, $S'_\lambda$-modules $M_\lambda$ with semilinear transition maps $m_{\mu\lambda}:M_\lambda\to M_\mu$ and semilinear maps $\nu_\lambda:M_\lambda\to M$ (over $s'_{\mu\lambda}$, resp. $\kappa'_\lambda$) compatible with them, such that: $S'$ is the colimit of the rings $S'_\lambda$ and $M$ the colimit of the abelian groups $M_\lambda$ over $\Lambda_2$; $S'_\lambda$ is essentially of finite type over $S_\lambda$ via $\sigma_\lambda$; $M_\lambda$ is the cokernel of a $S'_\lambda$-linear map $S'^{\oplus s}_\lambda\to S'^{\oplus t}_\lambda$; for $\lambda\le\mu$ in $\Lambda_2$, $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to S'_\mu$ is a localization and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'_\mu\to M_\mu$ an isomorphism; and $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to S'$ is a localization and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'\to M$ an isomorphism (clauses (1)-(5) of that node, with the maps $x\otimes y\mapsto\bar x\,y$ written there).

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), first paragraph: 'For some $\lambda_2\ge\lambda_1$ there exist $g_{j,\lambda_2}$ ... such that $S'=\colim_{\lambda\ge\lambda_2}S'_\lambda$ ...', the presentation matrix $A$ of $M$ descended to $A_{\lambda_3}$ and $M_\lambda=\operatorname{Coker}(A_\lambda)$ for $\lambda\ge\lambda_3$ (the matrix lies in $\mathrm{Mat}(t\times s,S'_{\lambda_3})$; the source's '$S_{\lambda_3}$' is a misprint), and the first sentence of the second paragraph ('With these choices ... is a localization ... is an isomorphism'); the construction of Lemma Tag 00QX (line 32427) over the system $S_\lambda$

proof.text: (Restricting $R$ and $S$ to $\Lambda_2$.) Every $\lambda\in\Lambda$ has some $\lambda'\in\Lambda_2$ with $\lambda\le\lambda'$ (an upper bound of $\lambda,\lambda_2$), and likewise for $\lambda\in\Lambda_1$. Regard $\Lambda$ as the category $\mathcal I$ with one arrow $\mu\to\lambda$ when $\lambda\le\mu$; it is cofiltered since $\Lambda$ is nonempty and directed, and $\mathcal I^{\mathrm{op}}$ is the directed set $\Lambda$, on which $(R_\lambda,r_{\mu\lambda})$ is a functor. The full subcategory $\mathcal J=\Lambda_2$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory] (1). Hence the canonical map from the colimit of $(R_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_2}$ to $R$ (induced by the $\pi_\lambda$, $\lambda\in\Lambda_2$) is an isomorphism, i.e. $(R,(\pi_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_2})$ is a colimit of $(R_\lambda)_{\Lambda_2}$ in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. The same argument with $\Lambda_1$ in place of $\Lambda$ shows that $(S,(\kappa_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda_2})$ is a colimit of $(S_\lambda)_{\Lambda_2}$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00R7 (lemma-criterion-flatness-fibre, line 32992), first paragraph (all systems are taken over $\lambda\ge\lambda_3$ there)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Take the nonempty directed set $\Lambda_2$ and, for $\lambda\le\mu$ in $\Lambda_2$, the local rings $R_\lambda$, $S_\lambda$, $S'_\lambda$, the local homomorphisms $\rho_\lambda:R_\lambda\to S_\lambda$ (step 2) and $\sigma_\lambda:S_\lambda\to S'_\lambda$ (step 4), the transition maps $r_{\mu\lambda}$, $s_{\mu\lambda}$, $s'_{\mu\lambda}$, $m_{\mu\lambda}$, and the maps $\pi_\lambda$, $\kappa_\lambda$, $\kappa'_\lambda$, $\nu_\lambda$ to $R$, $S$, $S'$, $M$. All these ring maps are local (steps 1, 2, 4); the transition maps commute with $\rho$ and $\sigma$ ($s_{\mu\lambda}\rho_\lambda=\rho_\mu r_{\mu\lambda}$, $s'_{\mu\lambda}\sigma_\lambda=\sigma_\mu s_{\mu\lambda}$), the maps to $R,S,S'$ commute with $\alpha$, $\beta$ ($\kappa_\lambda\rho_\lambda=\alpha\pi_\lambda$, $\kappa'_\lambda\sigma_\lambda=\beta\kappa_\lambda$) and with the transition maps, and the $M$-maps are semilinear and compatible (steps 2, 4). Clause (1) of the statement is step 5 for $R$, $S$ and step 4 for $S'$, $M$; clause (2) is step 1 ($R_\lambda$ over $\mathbf Z$), step 2 ($S_\lambda$ over $R_\lambda$) and step 4 ($S'_\lambda$ over $S_\lambda$); clause (3) is step 4 (a cokernel of $S'^{\oplus s}_\lambda\to S'^{\oplus t}_\lambda$ is generated by the images of the $t$ basis vectors, so it is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]); clause (4) is step 2 for $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R_\mu\to S_\mu$ and step 4 for $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S_\mu\to S'_\mu$ and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'_\mu\cong M_\mu$; clause (5) is step 2 for $S_\lambda\otimes_{R_\lambda}R\to S$ and step 4 for $S'_\lambda\otimes_{S_\lambda}S\to S'$ and $M_\lambda\otimes_{S'_\lambda}S'\cong M$.

split_report.summary: Read the proof of 00R7 (line 32992) and the lemmas it builds on: 00QT (line 32219), 00QU (32273), 00QV (32346), Remark 00QW, 00QX (32427), 00QY, 00QZ, 00R0, 00R1 (32593), 00R6 (32723), 00F4 (540), Definition 'essentially of finite presentation' (12836); all tags checked in tags/tags (00QW is a Remark, 00QY the non-local 'no condition' lemma: neither is used). The statement is kept; every clause (1)-(5), the local maps and the semilinear module maps are what the citer lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre uses in its steps 3-11 (and what the hypotheses (a), (b) of lem-weil-pbc-colimit-eventually-flat need). Not a Mathlib leaf (B8): Mathlib has no essentially-of-finite-presentation notion; searches added. Proof in 6 steps following the source: the base system R = colim R_lambda (new node lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-colimit-essentially-finite-type-over-z, 00QU's construction); the 00QV/00QX construction over a GIVEN directed system of local rings (new node lem-weil-pbc-limit-module-essentially-finite-presentation-over-system), applied first to R -> S over the R_lambda with the zero module, then to S -> S' with M over the S_lambda; between them the fact that S' is essentially of finite presentation over S (new node lem-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-presentation-over-intermediate, the localized analogue of 00F4 (4), which the source uses without statement); restriction of R and S to the final cofinal index set via lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory; and the assembly of clauses (1)-(5). Source: the descended presentation matrix lies in Mat(t x s, S'_lambda3), not S_lambda3 (misprint).
